title: HPO objective honors holdout fold — baseline receipt under PR-031 semantics
purpose: Document the post-PR-031 RMSE on the crypto_breakout_h3 baseline using the same TOML config + master entropy + n_trials as PR-025 calibration. Quantifies the metric shift introduced by carving the HPO CV substrate down to splits[train]+splits[val] (PR-031, v0.3.0) from the pre-PR-031 full dataframe (PR-025 era).

data.hpo_substrate: splits[train] + splits[val] (PR-031 — first 85% of source rows by timestamp)
data.holdout: splits[test] (last 15% by timestamp; unseen by HPO)

comparison_to_pr025.interpretation: Substrate shrunk from 100% of source data (PR-025 era; pre-PR-031) to 85% under PR-031 (splits[train]+splits[val] only; splits[test] genuinely held out). PR-031 median RMSE is SLIGHTLY LOWER than PR-025 Position A median (~-0.93%); PR-031 best is HIGHER than PR-025 best (~+14%), consistent with the Phase 3 convention finding that HPO may be slightly suboptimal in a small-data regime. Spread within completed trials is tighter under PR-031 (3e-06 vs PR-025 Position A 6e-06). The 0.027101 median from PR-025 is NOT a regression target — it was measured against the OLD 100%-substrate semantics. PR-031 makes the holdout truly held out from HP search at the cost of HPO seeing 15% less data; this is the intended behavior change per Phase 3 research (AutoGluon tabular-essentials.html @ SHA f8c428cbbef3bc319ff3f7710f5900e65637f4c4; sklearn user guide §3.1; Optuna issue #2184).
